items.text: Firmly Establishing COMPANY’s expectation at the KOM
Timely availability of relevant inputs from COMPANY
Managing project stakeholders & their interest
Selection of sound technical, economical and environmental friendly solution
Optimization / Value Engineering
In time completion of the SERVICES without affecting safety and quality.
Precise and clear recommendations for the next phase of the PROJECT.
The process enclosed in Appendix-I explains our overall execution approach.

SERVICES will be executed in our Abu Dhabi Office. All major assignments will be handled by our local office in Abu Dhabi and resources from our global professional network will be utilized (as and when required).
A dedicated task force will be established to cater the need for PROJECT based on the scope and schedule requirement.

To perform the services, EC will bring to this project its experience and expertise of project management & engineering resources. EC’s proposed management strategy shall be based upon utilizing the substantial experience and expertise available within organization, project management systems and resources.

A dedicated project team will be assigned in ABU DHABI to perform the services. The nominated Project Team under the umbrella of Project Manager will be responsible for executing the Services in accordance with the deliverables & will perform of their tasks according to meet the project schedule.
A high priority will be placed on proper interface with COMPANY’s team throughout all stages of the project starting from the kick-off meeting towards the completion of the Project.
Project Manager

The nominated project manager has the overall responsibility to ensure that qualified engineers and designers, along with appropriate means, are available for the projects.  He will be closely working with Study Manager, Team Leads, Contracts, Interface as well as  Project Controls. His role involves active interaction with COMPANY’s nominated focal point and manage the stake holders as well. Critical to successful Project management involves maintaining Project alignment to the goals of the Project Execution Plan. The primary challenge of Project Team is to achieve all of the Project goals and objectives while honouring the preconceived constraints; resources, scope, time, and budget. The secondary challenge is to optimize the allocation of necessary inputs and integrate them to meet pre-defined objectives.
Senior Engineer
The Engineer, who can be a senior or intermediate level, functionally reports to the Discipline Team Leader and operationally to the Project Lead Engineer. The Engineer responsibilities include:
Planning of project activity  in consultation with the Project Lead Engineer;
Reviewing project and technical documents to fully understand the project scope of work;
Reviewing design deliverables in accordance with discipline procedures and project requirements, prior to formal issue;
Executing assigned tasks;
Providing required input to the Design team;
Communicating issues to the discipline team in a timely fashion.
Lead Designer
The Lead Designer, who can be a senior of intermediate designer, shall:
Works under the supervision of Engineer to produce complete design deliverables for the Project;
Works independently, while directing and checking the work of other designers;
Assigns tasks to Designers according to their capabilities, to ensure that all the work produced by the design team is in accordance with the company’s established standards and Client requirements;
Assures that the design complies with applicable Engineering codes & standards.
Designer

The Designer shall work under the general supervision of the Lead Designer or Engineer, as applicable, in accordance with established procedures, to produce design deliverables from sketches or from engineering and design information.
Following contract signature, EC will initiate a robust project management approach to the project. The project manager will:
Prepare the planning package that will define the main tasks, deliverables. The planning package will include the deliverables register, project schedule and an outline of the execution plan.
Undertake an internal project kick-off meeting of all staff involved in the project and brief them on:
An overview of the Project,
The project’s objectives and deliverables,
The volume of work and the timescales,
Allocate individual responsibilities with specific deadlines,
Distribute copies of project brief to project team.
Arrange internal progress meetings.
Set up monthly invoicing procedures.

The project management and engineering team will be mobilised within two weeks after the project award and subject to COMPANY approval of the resources. The activities will, in general, be in accordance with approved EC’s QA procedures and the approved project QA plan.
The project activities will commence with a kick-off meeting to be held in EC’s Abu Dhabi office / COMPANY’s Abu Dhabi office. The purpose of the kick-off meeting will be to define:
Restatement of the scope of work and services required,
Establishment of communications protocol,
Agree drawing and document formats,
Clarify outstanding technical queries,
Review project schedule,
Agree on progress reporting requirements,
Arrangement of site visit dates (if required)
Obtain all available relevant documents drawings and data of existing facilities.

The data can form the starting point for the ENGINEERING  CONTRACTOR’s  Design Basis  and should be  cross  checked  for  various  design data  provided elsewhere. All pertinent data should be verified for potential conflicts by the  ENGINEERING CONTRACTOR prior to commencement of FEED as part of scope.
ENGINEERING CONTRACTOR shall complete a Basic Engineering Design Data  Specification, for use during the FEED and inclusion in the EPC RFT package.

Following the kick-off meeting, EC shall forward relevant requests to COMPANY to enable security passes to be obtained for the site visit and data collection exercise of the proposed facilities and tie-in locations etc.
A representative from the project management team will lead the site visit(s) supported by the relevant discipline engineers. The aim of the site visit(s) includes:
Familiarisation with the existing field operation and site details,
Review of existing operator documentation (provided at kick-off meeting),
Collect and review as-built drawings and document relevant to this work.
On return from the site visits, EC will produce a site visit report for COMPANY review. This will then create a working document for the survey (if any) and subsequent engineering activities.

PROJECT Control and Reporting will be executed in accordance with EC’s PROJECT Control Procedures, to be defined in the early stage of the PROJECT.
The Report formats and content are in accordance with the PROJECT Control Procedures. The Report formats shall be agreed with the COMPANY.
The EC will issue Weekly and Monthly progress reports as per Scope of Work.

The weekly progress report will be submitted every  week to COMPANY on the first working day of the following week, with progress cut-off ~ last working day of the week. For the weeks which coincides with the schedule of monthly report, the weekly report will not be issued. Contents of weekly report will be as follows:
Brief  narratives  of  the  activities  performed,  by  each  discipline, during the week.
Areas of concerns and proposed corrective actions.
Activities planned for next week.
List of documents and correspondence issued during the week.

The monthly progress report with cut-off ~ last Friday of each month, will be submitted on 6th working day of the following month to COMPANY. Content of the Monthly Progress Report will be agreed during the KOM.
EC will prepare Project Schedule which shall be reviewed and agreed with the COMPANY
Identified Engineering Services Milestones shall be included in Project Schedule
Overall “S” Curve shall be prepared (Planned vs Earned)
The following change control activities will be performed to facilitate the process by Project Controls:
Developing change control templates, incorporating project specific requirements
Setting the baseline
Identifying and classifying changes
Documenting changes
Estimating change impacts: TIC cost and schedule
Logging changes
Preparing change notices and change orders
Expediting change routing and approvals to ensure efficiency and continuity of project execution
Releasing approved changes; with implementation instruction for the various discipline and project controls systems.

At the end of each project, Project Close out report will be prepared. The main objective of this report is to prepare lessons learnt summary for next project. This will give a continuous learning in developing the organization.
The main content of this report is;
Project Introduction
Organization Charts
Variance Charts for Schedule, Man-hours and Cost (Budget vs Actual)
Deviations from initial Scope and reasons
Lessons Learnt and future recommendations
Profitability (for internal use only)

EC has an avid experience of delivering cost estimates at Pre-study, Feasibility, FEED for TIC (Total Investment Cost). Cost Estimation will be in-line with AACE.
Cost Estimate Reports (±40%) for SELECT Phase
Each stage of Cost estimate has its own maturity level of deliverables, definitions, reason for end usage, estimating methodology and accuracy range.
The salient deliverables for Cost estimation are;
Economic Analysis (for all alternatives)
Cost Estimating Plan
Cost Estimate Basis
Cost Estimate Summary
Cost Estimation Details
Risk Analysis
EC will address the cost breakdown listed below as minimum:
Location wise
Project Phases (Home ofﬁce, Procurement, Construction etc.).
COMPANY scope
EC shall submit cost estimation preparation plan as part of cost estimate methodology. Cost estimation preparation plan should include the following as a minimum:
Cost estimate methodology preparation / submission including COMPANY review cycle.
Budgetary quotation request preparation, evaluations.
Cost Risk Analysis simulation.
Draft Cost estimate preparation / submission and COMPANY review cycle (to be issued at least 3 weeks ahead of ﬁnal cost estimate submission including two weeks for COMPANY review).
Final cost estimate preparation / submission integrating COMPANY comments

Contracts/ Subcontracts and Procurement activities will be executed according to the defined Scope of Services as part of the PROJECT execution. The activities shall include all relevant work required to complete the SERVICES to ensure that all necessary information, details, studies, surveys, drawings and documents are available
Procurement support services anticipated as per the scope of work include:
Preparation of Sub-ENGINEERING CONTRACTOR (HAZOP Study) for the services to be performed during PROJECT.
Procurement & Selection of Sub-ENGINEERING CONTRACTORs (HAZOP Study) as required.
Preparation of Vendor List for the project in conjunction with COMPANY
Assistance in the preparation of ITT package

All interfaces with vendors, which involve obtaining quotation/purchase of equipment and/or materials, will be through Procurement team. Also, Technical Queries will be submitted to Vendors through Procurement team and response received will be forwarded to Engineering team accordingly.
All received information / Data from Sub-Contractor will be incorporated in the design documents.
Communication strategy is based on COMPANY’s expectations and EC’s commitment to create a transparent flow of information between the CONTRACT parties.
Close interaction during the PROJECT execution is essential and will be developed with mutual interaction at Site and other relevant locations.
Target is to ensure fluent flow of information in every execution level and location with proper tools, confidential environment and applying properly the communication principles in every occasion.
During the Kick off Meeting the Focal Points between the parties will be defined.
PROJECT communication and correspondence nomenclature shall be arranged according to the COMPANY procedure.
Communication shall be executed mainly by the following means:
Formal correspondence
E-mail correspondence
Face-to-face meetings
Teleconferences and dedicated video conference meetings

Correspondence process and principles between focal points of the EC and the COMPANY will be agreed in the Kick off Meeting and shown in the PROJECT Communication and PROJECT Correspondence process will be discussed at early stage of the PROJECT.

Meetings, workshops, interactive sessions will be arranged as agreed to enhance and develop our mutual understanding in order to acquire the valuable inputs to merge and incorporate with our experiences and common practices.
Official meeting program and schedule will be mutually agreed with the COMPANY during the Kick off Meeting.
PROJECT Meetings to be held:
Monthly Progress Review Meetings
Top level Steering Meetings
The EC is committed to provide high-quality technical, engineering and PROJECT services to attain sound and proven high quality standards.

The EC strives for the highest quality of operations and products in accordance with the requirements and expectations of our customers. Top management, superiors and every employee within the EC’s organization are responsible for ensuring quality in our business.
Our goal is Zero non-conformities.
Our way is – continuous improvement and lessons learned implemented in practice.

Every employee in the EC organization is responsible that his/her activity complies to the EC Quality and HSE policy. Each person is responsible for the quality of his/her performance and for controlling environmental impacts and safety issues.
Each EC’s line manager is responsible for resolving any Quality and HSE issues in his/her area of operations.
The role of the EC’s - Quality manager is to support the line and PROJECT organizations in avoiding any HSE and Quality issues.
Nominated PROJECT Manager is responsible for the Quality of the PROJECT.
The quality targets for the PROJECT are:
To meet the safety requirements set by the COMPANY
To meet the quality requirements set by the COMPANY
To meet the technical requirements set by the COMPANY
The PROJECT will be completed according to the budget and schedule.
EC is planned to conduct one (1) Internal Quality Audits’s during the execution of the Project.

Implementation of the system shall be in accordance with the EC’s Quality Manual and project specific Quality Plan. A well-defined and documented Quality Policy signed by Management shall be submitted demonstrating the EC’s commitment to the Quality Requirements.
Accredited Certification Body DNV Certification Oy/Ab (S001) has certified the operations of EC. The EC’s certified Management System will be applied in the PROJECT according to EC’s Quality Manual.

Additional to above proposed, QA/QC Audit & Quality Requirements will be aligned and followed as per COMPANY's Requirements and procedures. Please refer to relevant sections of the technical bid for EC’s QA/QC documents.

EC is committed to apply the HSE policy and principles and specially to apply technologies and PROJECT management and implementation practices, which have been proven sound in terms of health, safety and environment.
This entails that
The HSE impacts of the technology suggested to a customer are known
The risks are within acceptable limits
We follow the highest level of requirement concerning legislation and the customer’s own norms
High standard construction safety can be obtained through good PROJECT performance and safety practices in construction phase
Our Goal:
Zero incidents. We believe that all accidents are preventable.
We put the personal health and safety of our employees and co-operation partners first
Our Way:

It is how we do business and it is how we live. Our people are our greatest asset and the basis for our success. We believe that we owe it to our employees and co-operation partners to help keep them safe and healthy.
High-quality HSE performance in the PROJECT shall be ensured by:
PROJECT Management commitment

Excellent basic professional HSE competence of all discipline personnel and specific competence of HSE responsible persons, emphasizing knowledge of local and the COMPANY rules and regulations, ADNOC/COMPANY specifications and COP's.
Continuously measuring, analyzing and developing our PROJECT HSE practices and procedures
Proper introduction of PROJECT personnel into PROJECT HSE requirements
Additional to above proposed, HSE Requirements will be aligned and followed as per COMPANY's Requirements and procedures.

During execution of the project, following two (2) major categories of document will be produced;
Project Administration & Correspondence Documents such as correspondence, minutes of meeting, transmittals, site queries, project change control, and etc.
Technical Documents such as Engineering documents, drawings, technical specifications, and etc.
The above two (2) document groups will be managed and controlled according to the ‘Project Coordination Plan’ and ‘Document Management and Control Plan’.
Final document dossier shall include all documents and drawings prepared by the EC for the PROJECT, including (but not limited to):
Softcopies in native format (AutoCad, E database, with Latest Edition) shall be submitted for all drawings & documents.
Final Consultancy Completion Dossier shall include all documents prepared by the EC.
Final Dossier Index shall be submitted for COMPANY approval prior to compiling the documents and handing over.
Upon completion and approval of all amendments to the Tender Documents shall be submitted to COMPANY
The execution approach below shows how the SERVICES move from contract award to close-out, with COMPANY review and approval at each stage.

items.section: Early phase – contract award and mobilisation
items.text: Contract signed; kick-off meeting (safety moment, common project objectives, project scope, schedule, milestones, initial data received and further data requirements, project organisation, project team working methods, reporting and communication matrix) with agenda and minutes of meeting; mobilisation of the team; planning package preparation and COMPANY approval; project execution and quality plan preparation and COMPANY approval.

items.section: Doing phase – data acquisition and site visit
items.text: Data acquisition, existing data and native files; site visit after LOA and CNIA pass readiness; site visit report and COMPANY approval; review of all data received for the development works; interface with ongoing projects.

items.section: Doing phase – STUDY / FEED works and deliverables
items.text: Project design basis; process works; HSE / loss prevention works; piping / pipeline works; civil / structural works; electrical works; mechanical works; instrumentation and control works; MTOs and BOQs for all disciplines; inputs such as HSE studies, NDT testing, topographical / underground survey report, OEM adequacy report, CP design and FIV.

Cost estimate methodology preparation and COMPANY approval; database for bulk items and local (UAE) construction and maintenance cost; cost of all long-lead items from vendors / OEMs; cost estimate preparation and submission.
Draft engineering package submission; COMPANY comments incorporated; final engineering package and COMPANY approval; STUDY / FEED dossier submission.
Project close-out report; EPC scope of work; implementation schedule Level II; ITB preparation; lessons learned and readiness for the next phase.
